items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: one of my favorite moments was when we had five sets going, me and Tony and Eric and Nicholas and my dad, all playing

ctx.x: So how did your mother feel about having five drum sets in the house?

She was accepting. You know? But one of my favorite moments was when we had five sets going, me and Tony and Eric and Nicholas and my dad, all playing — or actually my dad wasn’t there, he was off in his studio I think, but the four sets of drums were going and my mother was playing piano and we were playing “Willow Weep for Me.” She was pretty good. And something else she would play, “When Sunny Gets Blue” but the four guys, I think I might have been 15 and then the ages range on down. And everybody was into Led…

whoever it was. And usually the sets were scattered. Everybody had their set in their room but if there was a rehearsal or a jam session or something like that we’d bring down all the sets so there would be five sets set up and an acoustic piano.
